mechanism_fidelity.rationale: Repeated A-B measurements, demand stratification, comparison with the historical low-demand baseline, and low-demand follow-up preserve the temporal-pattern-to-state-inference chain. Separating the known two-hour intake effect addresses changing observation conditions. Sampling and mix limitations remain explicit, and persistence is not treated as component localization.

target_fidelity.rationale: Establishing whether excess delay persists on A-B provides an explicitly bounded contribution to locating delay and prioritizing investigation. The mapping does not identify a unique team or establish which changes would reduce delay, and it does not claim to answer those portions of the question.

operational_coherence.rationale: Route, demand slot, and endpoint wait are observable. Stratified repeated waits can reveal whether elevation relative to the low-demand baseline persists beyond the known busy-slot intake effect. Four initial observations and two follow-up observations fit the trial and slot budgets, with initial and follow-up evaluation fitting two analysis passes. The inference remains bounded to the observed path and period.

validity.rationale: The mapping preserves serial monitoring and supplies an operationally supported, explicitly limited contribution to the retained target question. Its validity does not require unique component localization or an established remedy because neither is claimed.

uncertainty: The proposed observations have not been supplied, so persistence is a possible finding rather than an established result.
A-B endpoint observations cannot determine which internal team contributes the excess delay.
The procedure does not establish an effective staffing or handoff change, and testbed findings require separate assessment before live application.
